title: Sample 14-10: Conclusion of Play

illustrates.quote: A phrase indicating the conclusion of the play (e.g., “The End” or “The Curtain Falls,” etc.) is centered and preceded and followed by a blank line.

blocks.speaker: Webster
blocks.text: **Webster** (moving to center stage, and joining *Jabez'* hands and *Mary’s).* And whom God hath joined let no man put asunder. (He kisses *Mary* and turns, dusting his hands.) Well, that job’s done. I hope there’s pie for breakfast, neighbor Stone.
(And, as some of the women, dancing, bring in pies from the kitchen)

print.notes: The speaker name 'Webster' is bold (retained, 14.1.3); the two parenthetical stage directions embedded within Webster's own dialogue keep the character names 'Jabez'’/’Mary’s’/’Mary’ in italics for distinction (14.4.1c), with the rest of each parenthetical plain; the closing paren and full stop right after ‘Mary’s’ are kept INSIDE that same italic run since they sit with no space before the next word (confirmed by forward translation: keeping them italic reproduces the given braille's own single italic-word indicator with no separate terminator, exactly like Example 14-4's ‘hysterically:’). The standalone stage direction between Webster's speech and the closing phrase drops its own italics entirely, per the ordinary 'stage' default (14.5.3c/14.4.1c — no distinction needed here, unlike the embedded names above). 'THE CURTAIN FALLS' is printed in full capitals — built as a centred heading (14.8.1), blank line before and after (formatHeading's own default for a centred/level-1 heading, no special-casing needed).
print.printFeatures: Bold speaker name; two parenthetical, partly-italicised stage directions embedded in the dialogue; a standalone (non-embedded) stage direction; a centred, all-caps closing phrase.

resolution: A/B agreed on braille (byte-for-byte) and on print substance; both described the bold/italic emphasis only in prose `features` fields (B) or left it out of `text` (A) rather than marking it in place. Per this repo's own established convention, `text` was rewritten with **Webster**/*Jabez'*/*Mary's).*'/*Mary* embedded directly — the exact italic-run boundary (including the closing paren and period right after ‘Mary’s’) was determined by forward-translation testing until an EXACT MATCH was reached, matching Example 14-4's own already-documented italic-terminator behaviour. A's own illustrates.rule/quote (14.8.1, the actual rule text) kept over B's own null/title-repeat. Forward-translated through Emboss's translator (one {type:'play',subtype:'prose'} block with bold/italic segments, one {type:'stage'} block, one centred {type:'heading'} block): EXACT MATCH (see differences.md).
